plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 5.2.6
plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates the slicing method for computing the volume of a solid of known cross-sectional area. Left panel: a solid S extending along the x-axis from x = a to x = b, divided into n slabs S1, S2, ..., Sn by partition points a = x0, x1, ..., x_{n-1}, b = xn marked along the base axis; one slab is highlighted in blue. Right panel (zoom): the kth slab Sk is isolated and shown as a right prism with width Delta_xk along the x-axis; a caption reads The cross section here has area A(x*_k). An arrow connects the two views. The figure sets up the Riemann sum sum A(x*_k) Delta_xk as an approximation for the total volume, whose limit gives the definite integral V = integral from a to b of A(x) dx.

elements: horizontal x-axis (left panel) with arrowhead, tick labels a, x1, x2, ..., x_{n-1}, b
solid S: a prism along x whose top is a rising concave ridge (height h(x)), constant depth into the page, drawn semi-transparent red with red outline
front curved profile edge of S (the dome ridge in the page plane)
right end-cap face of S at x=b (a cross-section, red outline)
n-1 interior partition planes perpendicular to the x-axis, drawn as thin black vertical/oblique outlines dividing S into slabs S1..Sn
slab labels S1, S2 near the left and Sn near the right on the front face
one highlighted slab (index k) filled translucent blue with darker blue edges
large curved beige arrow sweeping from the left solid toward the right zoom panel
right zoom panel: isolated kth slab Sk as a thin right prism (width Δx_k along x, height h(x*_k), full depth), translucent blue with black front vertical edge
right panel x-axis with arrowhead, point marker x*_k (dot) and a bracketed interval labelled Δx_k with inward arrows
label Sk on the right face of the zoomed slab
beige rounded callout box reading 'The cross section here has area A(x*_k).' with a pointer arrow to the slab's cross-section face
numeric readout text: A(x*_k) value, Δx_k value, slab volume A(x*_k)·Δx_k, total Riemann sum Σ A(x*_k)Δx_k, and exact volume ∫A dx

interactions.label: Number of slabs n
interactions.teaches: Increasing n multiplies the partition of S into thinner slabs; the Riemann sum Σ A(x*_k)Δx_k visibly tightens and converges to the exact integral V = ∫_a^b A(x) dx

interactions.label: Selected slab k (drag the zoom)
interactions.teaches: Dragging k moves the highlighted slice along x and updates the zoomed prism, revealing how the cross-sectional area A(x*_k) and the single slab volume A(x*_k)·Δx_k change with position

demo_steps.title: Coarse partition
demo_steps.narration: With n=6 the solid is cut into a few thick slabs; the highlighted blue slab k=3 is pulled out at right as a prism of width Δx_k and cross-section A(x*_k). The sum is a rough estimate of the volume.

demo_steps.title: Move the slice
demo_steps.narration: Drag k toward b. The cross-section grows taller (h(x) increases), so A(x*_k) and the slab volume increase — the slice's contribution depends on where it sits.

demo_steps.title: Refine to convergence
demo_steps.narration: Raise n to 40. The slabs become thin sheets, the blue highlight narrows, and Σ A(x*_k)Δx_k approaches the exact integral — the limit that defines V = ∫_a^b A(x) dx.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: left panel x-axis spans x∈[0,4] (a=0,b=4) mapped to world X∈[0,4]; constant depth D=1.2 along the oblique receding axis (+Z diagonal up-right); cross-section at x is a rectangle of height h(x) and depth D, with h(x)=0.35+1.1*sqrt(x/4) (rising concave ridge, ~0.35 at a to ~1.45 at b). Thus A(x)=D*h(x) and exact V=∫_0^4 D*h(x)dx = D*(0.35*4 + 1.1*(2/3)*4^1.5/ sqrt(4)*...) — compute numerically in code. Left solid occupies X∈[0,4], Y∈[0,1.5], Z∈[0,1.2]. Right zoom panel offset to X∈[6.5,9.5]; its single slab width = Δx_k = 4/n placed at the partition cell containing k, height h(x*_k) with midpoint sample x*_k. Partition planes are vertical oblique rectangles at x_i=i*4/n. Colors: solid fill #f6c0bd @0.55 opacity, edges #cc3333; highlighted/zoom slab fill #8fc0ea @0.6, edges #1f5fa8; axes/labels black #111; callout box #f6e3b0 with #d9b95c border; arrow #e8d9a8. Readout panel top-right shows A(x*_k), Δx_k, slab vol, Σ sum, exact V to 3 decimals.
interactionPlan.notes: Oblique projection: draw each cross-section rectangle in the Y-Z plane then extrude along X; render the receding depth as a fixed screen diagonal (e.g. offset (cos35°,sin35°)*depth) so front faces stay true rectangles. Rebuild slab geometry on every n change (dispose old meshes); move/recolor only the highlighted slab and the zoom prism on k change. Use midpoint rule x*_k=(x_{k-1}+x_k)/2. Clamp k to [1,n]. Keep both panels in one scene (the zoom is an inset linked by the arrow), updating the zoom reactively rather than toggling views. Render text via canvas-texture sprites or an HTML overlay for crisp labels (a, x1, b, S, Sk, A(x*_k), Δx_k, readouts).

authoredContext:
Let S be a solid that extends along the x-axis and is bounded on the left and right, respectively, by the planes that are perpendicular to the x-axis at x = a and x = b (Figure 5.2.5). Find the volume V of the solid, assuming that its cross-sectional area A(x) is known at each x in the interval [a, b]. To solve this problem we begin by dividing the interval [a, b] into n subintervals, thereby dividing the solid into n slabs as shown in the left part of Figure 5.2.6. If we assume that
the width of the kth subinterval is _x000b_xk, then the volume of the kth slab can be approximated
by the volume A(x∗
k )_x000b_xk of a right cylinder of width (height) _x000b_xk and cross-sectional area
A(x∗
k ), where x∗
k is a point in the kth subinterval (see the right part of Figure 5.2.6).
